title: Fort Knox - The Vault Nobody Has Seen

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
This is the most secure building on Earth.
Everyone in the country knows the name.
Almost nobody has ever been inside.
It holds the gold of other nations.
Not only the gold of America.
It sits in the hills of Kentucky.
A long low building made of brick.
From the road it looks like a school.
It is not a school at all.
This is Fort Knox, Kentucky.
Work began there in 1939.
The building was finished in 1944.
Five years of poured concrete and stone.
The roof was modelled on Gothic halls.
Vaulted stone arches above the corridors.
Europe, rebuilt in the middle of Kentucky.
The doors mattered more than the roof.
The main door weighs about 56 tons.
It is reportedly the heaviest vault door made.
A round steel face, cropped by the frame.
It swings on a solid steel hinge.
Steel plate, then concrete, then more steel.
The concrete runs right through the walls.
The walls are thicker than the doors.
A castle built to outlast a siege.
The gold sits on nine floors.
Rows of bars stacked to the ceiling.
The reserve ran into the hundreds of billions.
At its peak it weighed 12,000 tonnes.
The stacks filled whole wings of it.
Much of that gold belongs to other governments.
Small national flags above one vault door.
The vault holds their gold as well.
Only a small share stays on site.
Only a few hundred tonnes remain.
The rest was moved out years ago.
A visitor counter, a ledger, a stamp.
Thousands of people tour it every year.
School field trips arrive each spring.
A line of children in a corridor.
They walk above the stored gold.
They never walk below the gold.
The inner doors stay bolted shut.
Almost nobody alive has seen inside.

beats.line: Everyone in the country knows the name.

beats.line: Almost nobody has ever been inside.
beats.visual: character shrugging at a chained gate, hands turned up; speech bubble 'been inside? no.'

beats.line: It holds the gold of other nations.
beats.visual: open vault interior, long ranks of gold bars receding to the back wall

beats.line: Not only the gold of America.
beats.visual: same vault, but the bars carry many small national flags on their ends; character pointing at them

beats.line: It sits in the hills of Kentucky.
beats.visual: hand-drawn map of Kentucky, one dot marked in the north-central hills; label 'KENTUCKY'

beats.line: A long low building made of brick.
beats.visual: long low brick building seen from the road, filling the full width of the frame, flat roofline

beats.line: From the road it looks like a school.
beats.visual: the same building drawn with school windows and a bell tower; character standing small at the door

beats.line: It is not a school at all.
beats.visual: the school windows and bell peel away, steel vault plates and bolts underneath; character deadpan

beats.line: This is Fort Knox, Kentucky.
beats.visual: title card, hand-lettered 'FORT KNOX' stamped across a gold bar, Kentucky outline behind it

beats.line: Work began there in 1939.
beats.visual: old calendar page, the year 1939 circled in red pencil; shovel and trowel beside it

beats.line: The building was finished in 1944.
beats.visual: calendar page beside it, 1944 circled, a line drawn between the two dates

beats.line: Five years of poured concrete and stone.
beats.visual: site under construction, concrete mixer, timber forms, workers as simple flat figures

beats.line: The roof was modelled on Gothic halls.
beats.visual: roof trusses being raised over the hall, Gothic pointed arches already set below them

beats.line: Vaulted stone arches above the corridors.
beats.visual: interior corridor, stone vaulted arches receding overhead, lamps on the floor casting flat pools

beats.line: Europe, rebuilt in the middle of Kentucky.
beats.visual: the corridor arch drawn beside a European cathedral arch, side by side, matching shapes

beats.line: The doors mattered more than the roof.
beats.visual: character pushing on a small steel door that does not move; speech bubble 'the doors matter'

beats.line: The main door weighs about 56 tons.
beats.visual: the round vault door drawn enormous, cropped by both frame edges; character tiny at its foot

beats.line: It is reportedly the heaviest vault door made.
beats.visual: the same door with a hand-lettered label '56 TONS' arced across it; character flattened against it

beats.line: A round steel face, cropped by the frame.
beats.visual: close on the door face: concentric steel rings, a wheel handle, deep bolt holes; character awed

beats.line: It swings on a solid steel hinge.
beats.visual: the hinge block alone, drawn huge, a thick steel pin running through it

beats.line: Steel plate, then concrete, then more steel.
beats.visual: door cross-section, layer by layer: steel plate, concrete, steel plate, each layer labelled

beats.line: The concrete runs right through the walls.
beats.visual: cross-section of the surrounding wall, concrete a solid mass past both frame edges

beats.line: The walls are thicker than the doors.
beats.visual: the wall mass drawn taller than the door beside it, one word stamped across it: 'THICKER'

beats.line: A castle built to outlast a siege.
beats.visual: the building drawn as a small castle with towers and an arrow slit

beats.line: The gold sits on nine floors.
beats.visual: cutaway of the building, nine stacked floors labelled, gold on each; character climbing the levels

beats.line: Rows of bars stacked to the ceiling.
beats.visual: gold bars stacked to the ceiling and past the top edge of the frame, rows going back

beats.line: The reserve ran into the hundreds of billions.
beats.visual: huge hand-lettered figure 'HUNDREDS OF BILLIONS' painted across the gold stacks

beats.line: At its peak it weighed 12,000 tonnes.
beats.visual: a scale comparison, a small car drawn under a gold bar; label 'about 1 kilo'

beats.line: The stacks filled whole wings of it.
beats.visual: the whole cutaway filled edge to edge with gold, no empty floor left showing

beats.line: Much of that gold belongs to other governments.
beats.visual: ledger page open on a desk, a long column of country names with weights beside them

beats.line: Small national flags above one vault door.
beats.visual: small national flags in a row painted along the wall above one vault door

beats.line: The vault holds their gold as well.
beats.visual: character nodding at the flag row; speech bubble 'not all of it is ours'

beats.line: Only a small share stays on site.
beats.visual: the full gold hall drawn, then the same hall drawn nearly bare; labels 'THEN' and 'TODAY'

beats.line: Only a few hundred tonnes remain.
beats.visual: a small cluster of bars alone in the middle of a wide empty floor; character small beside them

beats.line: The rest was moved out years ago.
beats.visual: an arrow leaving the building, drawn in outline, pointing off the right edge of the frame

beats.line: A visitor counter, a ledger, a stamp.
beats.visual: visitor counter with a ledger, an ink stamp, a guard desk in flat fills

beats.line: Thousands of people tour it every year.
beats.visual: a queue of visitor figures at the counter, drawn as simple shapes, no faces

beats.line: School field trips arrive each spring.
beats.visual: school bus parked outside, children as small flat figures filing toward the door

beats.line: A line of children in a corridor.
beats.visual: a line of children from behind in a long bright corridor, one hand on the wall

beats.line: They walk above the stored gold.
beats.visual: the corridor floor drawn in cutaway, gold stacks visible right beneath their feet

beats.line: They never walk below the gold.
beats.visual: the children stopped at a chained inner door; character holding a hand out, speech bubble 'not this way'

beats.line: The inner doors stay bolted shut.
beats.visual: the inner steel door shut, bolts drawn heavy across it, a red lamp above

beats.line: Almost nobody alive has seen inside.
beats.visual: night exterior, the building almost black, one gold-lit archway; character alone in the foreground, flat mouth, speech bubble 'never seen'
